transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I guess it's about my wrist. I have this scar on it. I know it's probably not as bad as I think it is, but... when I'm out, like at church or playing bridge, I just feel like everyone is looking right at it. Like it's the only thing they see when they look at me.
Do you think about the scar on your wrist when you're alone?
Well... I suppose it crosses my mind. I'm not really sure how often, though. I just try to keep busy.
Has your concern about the scar on your wrist affected your relationships or daily activities in any way?

Well... maybe a little. I do bookkeeping, and... I suppose I've been a bit late turning some of my work in recently. And I guess I’ve skipped a few things... like choir, and my theater volunteer commitments. I just... I get so caught up trying to make sure my wrist won’t be noticed before I go anywhere.
Is it just your wrist with the scar that you're concerned about people noticing, or are there other parts of your body you worry about as well?
No, it's... really just the scar. I don't... I don't worry about anything else like that. Just my wrist.
How much distress would you say the scar on your wrist causes you?
I'm not really sure... I don't know if "distress" is the word I would use. It just... bothers me, I guess. I don't really know how to measure it. I just prefer to keep it hidden.
How long have you been bothered by the scar on your wrist?
I don't know... a while, I suppose. I haven't really kept track.
Have you ever wished you could change anything else about your appearance?
No, not really. I don't... I don't really think about that sort of thing much. Just what we already talked about.
Do you think people are staring at the scar because of how it looks or because they might be wondering what happened to you?

I don't know... I suppose they might wonder what happened. But... I just feel like it's the first thing they notice. Even if it's not as bad as I think it is. When I'm at church, or playing bridge... it just feels like everyone's eyes go right to it.
Is it the way the scar looks that bothers you, or is it more about what people might think happened to you because of the scar?
I'm not really sure... I haven't thought about it quite like that. I suppose I just... I just don't like the way it looks. It's just bothersome, that's all.
Is it more bothersome to you that people might see the scar itself, or that they might ask you about how you got it?
I... I really couldn't say. I guess probably just them seeing it. People don't usually ask me about it anyway, so... I just prefer it if it wasn't noticed. It's just uncomfortable.
Is it the appearance of the scar itself that bothers you, or what the scar might imply or represent to others?
I... I don't really know what you mean by what it represents. Like I said, it's just... I just don't care for the look of it. I don't think it's really any deeper than that.
Is it more bothersome to you that people might notice the scar because of how it looks or because they might wonder how you got it?
I just... I think we've covered this. It's just the way it looks. I don't really know why we keep going over it. I just don't like people seeing it.
Do you think your reaction to the scar is stronger than how most people would react if they had a similar scar?

I don't really know about other people. I... I suppose I know the scar on my wrist probably isn't as bad as it looks to me. But... well, when I'm at church, or playing bridge, I just keep feeling like everyone's eyes go right to it. Like it's the very first thing they notice about me now. So... I don't know if that's a stronger reaction or not.
Do you think your concern about the scar is out of proportion to how noticeable it actually is to others?

I... well, like I just said, I suppose I know it's probably not as glaring to everyone else as it is to me. But... it just feels like it is. When I'm dealing cards at bridge, or sitting in a pew, I just can't shake the feeling that they're all staring right at my wrist. So... maybe it is out of proportion. I'm really not sure.
Do you think you would feel better about the scar if you were certain that other people didn't notice it?
I... I don't know. Maybe. I just... I just don't like it. I don't really want to talk about what other people think anymore.
Would your concern about the scar decrease if you could be certain that people wouldn't ask you any questions about how you got it?
I'm... I'm not sure. I suppose it might help a little, but... I just don't like the scar. I'd rather just not talk about this anymore.
Is your main concern that the scar is unattractive or that it might lead to questions about your past?
I... I just think it's ugly. That's really all it is. I don't... I don't want to talk about this part anymore, please.
Is there something specific about your past that you are trying to keep private by hiding the scar?
No. I just... I told you, I just think it's ugly. There's no big secret. I just don't like how it looks. Can we please move on from this?
Is there anything about how you got the scar that you're trying to keep private?
No. I... I thought I just answered that. There isn't anything. I really don't have anything else to say about it.
Is there something about the scar that bothers you beyond just how it looks?
I don't know how many different ways I can say it. No. It's just... it's just the way it looks. There isn't anything else to it.
